newsitem.title: USA: Sears sees 860 full-line stores by 2000.
newsitem.headline: Sears sees 860 full-line stores by 2000.

text.p: Sears Roebuck & Co on Wednesday said it planned to open 131 new full-line stores by 2000, while closing 70 existing outlets.
That would raise the total number of full-line stores operated by the company to 860 from 821 at the end of 1996, the company said.
Of the new stores, the company will open 66 of them in new markets, while 65 will replace older stores, Sears officials told analysts at a meeting in Chicago.
Overall, Sears plans to spend $1.7 billion in domestic capital expenditures in 1997, up from about $1.6 billion in 1996, Chief Financial Officer Alan Lacy said.
In the full-line stores, Sears was looking for growth in new and underdeveloped product lines, said Bob Mettler, president of merchandising.
Those include petite apparel, fine jewelry, footwear, women's jeans, ethnically diverse merchandise, women's suits, men's suit separates, cosmetics, cameras and cookware.
Sears this year expects to begin selling CRB Khakis men's causal wear and Mosaics, a line of clothing targeted toward African-American women, Mettler said.
Sears is also opening a national gift registry at all its stores in 1997, he said.
